newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium business has to watch environment issue.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium business has to watch environment issue.

text.p: The aluminium industry has to be aware of environmental concerns, as this may become a key factor for end-use buyers, Per-Olof Aronson Vice-Chairman of Sweden's Granges AB said.
Aluminium is usually seen as environmentally-friendly, because it has favourable physical properties.
"The negative environmental impact of aluminium stems from the alumina refineries and the smelters," Aronson said at the Financial Times World Aluminium Conference.
Most modern aluminium plants run on hydro or nuclear power and are highly effective in terms of energy consumption and the environmental impact.

"However, as we all know, a large proportion of global production takes place in smelters based on burning low-grade fossil fuel using ineffecient technology and inadequate emission control," Aronson said in remarks prepared for delivery at the conference.
Buyers of semi-products specify physical properties very carefully and demand a just-in-time service.
In future, they may also demand a certificate for the environmental quality of the metal they buy.
"...this is an important issue which the aluminium industry should address," he added.
